questions.q: What materials did Early Man primarily use as 'paint' for their cave wall drawings?
options: Animal blood, plant sap, and colored earth
questions.explain: Early man relied on natural materials readily available in their environment, such as colored earth (ochre), animal blood, plant sap, and animal fat mixed with charcoal to create pigments for cave paintings.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which of the following is considered the most common subject matter in Early Man's cave paintings?
questions.explain: The predominant subject matter of early cave art was large wild animals, such as bison, horses, and deer, often depicted in hunting scenes. It is believed this was done for magical or religious purposes to ensure a successful hunt.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: ![Altamira Cave Painting](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8b/9_Bisonte_Magdaleniense_pol%C3%ADcromo.jpg)By Museo de Altamira y D. Rodríguez, CC BY-SA 3.0, Link The image above represents artwork from the Altamira caves. What period of human history is this kind of art associated with?
questions.explain: Cave paintings, such as those found in Altamira (Spain) and Lascaux (France), were created by Early Man during the Upper Paleolithic period (Old Stone Age).

questions.q: Why did Early Man most likely engage in artistic drawings deep inside dark caves?
options: To practice their drawing skills for schools
For magical, religious rituals and to record hunting exploits
To sell the drawings to neighboring tribes
questions.explain: Historians and archaeologists believe that early man drew deep in caves primarily for magical and religious rituals, specifically 'sympathetic magic' designed to capture the animal's spirit and ensure a successful hunt.

questions.q: During which prehistoric era did early humans begin creating pottery as a form of functional art due to a shift towards agriculture?
questions.explain: The Neolithic Era (New Stone Age) brought about the Agricultural Revolution. As early humans settled down to farm, they needed containers to store grains and liquids, leading to the invention and aesthetic development of pottery.

questions.q: What tools did Early Man use for carving and engraving on rocks and bones?
questions.explain: Before the discovery of metals, Early Man used sharp stones, particularly flint, to scrape, carve, and engrave materials like wood, bone, and rock.

questions.q:
![Nok Terracotta](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e2/Nok_sculpture_Louvre_70-1998-11-1.jpg)

Look at the image of the terracotta head above. It features pierced eyes, nose, and mouth, which is characteristic of which ancient Nigerian art culture?
questions.explain: Nok Art is the oldest known terracotta culture in Nigeria (and Sub-Saharan Africa). Its sculptures are highly recognizable by the elaborate hairstyles and the pierced pupils, nostrils, and lips.

questions.q: Which Nigerian art culture is world-renowned for its highly naturalistic bronze and terracotta heads often associated with their ruling kings (Oonis)?
questions.explain: Ife art is famous for its naturalistic bronze, stone, and terracotta sculptures, many of which depict royalty or Oonis (kings of Ife). The naturalism is exceptionally high compared to other early African art.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design

questions.q: The traditional method used by the people of Benin and Ife to cast their intricate bronze sculptures is known as:
questions.explain: The 'cire-perdue' or lost-wax casting process involves making a wax model, covering it with clay, melting out the wax, and pouring molten bronze into the hollow space. It was widely used in ancient Benin and Ife bronze casting.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design

questions.q: Igbo-Ukwu art is historically significant in Nigeria because it contains the oldest known examples of which type of metalwork in West Africa?
questions.explain: Discovered in 1938, Igbo-Ukwu artifacts represent the earliest known examples of bronze casting in West Africa, dating back to the 9th century. They are noted for their intricate surface decoration and leaded bronze composition.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design

questions.q: The Esie art culture in Kwara State, Nigeria, is primarily noted for thousands of figures carved from which material?
questions.explain: Esie art represents the largest collection of stone images (specifically soapstone/steatite figures) discovered in sub-Saharan Africa. The figures depict human forms and were found in Kwara State.
